text: Lightning never strikes twice? This building gets hit over twenty times a year.
So why does lightning keep picking the same place?
A storm cloud fills up with electric charge.
To reach the ground, it sends a spark down in short jumps.
As it gets close, tall things send sparks up to meet it.
The first spark to touch it makes the path.
Then the bright flash rushes along that path.
A tall, pointed tower is the closest point to the cloud.
So it wins again and again.
The Empire State Building gets hit about twenty to twenty-five times a year.
So lightning does strike twice. It often strikes where the path is shortest.
